svg.title: DeiT-Tiny INT8 accelerator: system architecture on the Nexys A7
svg.desc: The host PC talks over a USB-UART to axi_host_bridge. The bridge writes weights and a run list to DDR2 through a SmartConnect and the MIG. An AXI DMA copies each phase from DDR2 into vit_axi_wrapper as a 64-bit stream. Inside matmul_engine a sequencer runs a table of descriptors on a pool of eight block-RAM buffers. Matmuls go through an 8 by 8 systolic array, a drain with bias and eight requantizers. Non-linear ops go through residual add, GELU, LayerNorm and softmax. Results return to the pool.
svg.text: System architecture on the Nexys A7-100T. Arrows are labelled with what they carry in one clock beat.
run_image.py: weights once, then image + RUN
weights, biases, descriptors, run list, image
XC7A100T · 20,854 LUT · 161 of 240 DSP · 112 of 135 BRAM tiles · 100 MHz, WNS +0.386 ns
busy, done, error, lost, DDR ready
host packets with CRC-16 → AXI transactions
RUN walks the run list in DDR2 on its own: LOAD, START, LOAD, START …
AXI registers and stream targets: pool, bias store, LayerNorm constants, descriptors
host port: pool 8 × int8 · bias 8 × int32 · LayerNorm 48b · descriptors 32b
fetches an op, loads the register bank,
runs one op after the other
walks a matmul tile by tile:
per-column bias, added in the drain
Buffer pool: 8 buffers × 8 banks, 230 KB as sized for 50 tokens. An op names its buffers, so nothing is copied.
skew B: lane i delayed by i cycles
1 DSP per PE, int8 × int8 → int32
one accumulator row or column per cycle, + bias
8 × int8 per cycle, 2 operands for add
op fields: which unit, which buffers, which table
ONE ENCODER LAYER = 26 OPS, IN THIS ORDER
LN1 → Q, K, V (×3 heads) → S = Q·Kᵀ (×3) → softmax (×3) → O = P·V (×3) → projection → residual add → LN2 → fc1 → GELU → fc2 → residual add
